rules.semantic_labels: Normalize only decorative edge whitespace; match the complete semantic title. Treat adjacent parameter titles and value-only buttons as separate elements unless the observed hierarchy combines them.
rules.foreground_scope: Resolve the current foreground container and element type before reading or acting. Do not infer an accessibility type from visible text; OS choices may be Buttons inside a CollectionView rather than StaticText. Review every remaining interaction, not just the failing line. Multi-selection may use Table Cells containing entity StaticText even when single-selection uses CollectionView Buttons; inspect the actual presenter. Native submenu leaf buttons can omit source IDs even when the parent menu exports its ID. When terminal hierarchy proves this, use the complete observed semantic title in the menu CollectionView/Cell/Button structure via menuActions/tapTestMenuAction; do not retry an absent ID or pick the first match.
rules.unique_reads_and_actions: Both passive reads and actions use one foreground-scoped match. Observations need a visible frame; actions additionally require enabled/hittable. Never pick the first duplicate. Source IDs may not be exported by native alert fields. For observed nested action wrappers, select direct children of the action container; containing a same-ID element is not proof of uniqueness. Keep hit testing in object readiness, not a literal query predicate. Run check-ui-query-predicates.py before CI. Native SwiftUI Switch rows can wrap a separate direct Switch child without an ID. Use setTestSwitch to act on the unique child and verify its value; a hittable labelled row does not establish the actual switch hit point.
rules.live_state: Require the expected live data or completed transition. Placeholder, redaction, and element existence alone do not establish readiness. Native empty TextField.value may equal placeholderValue: prove empty input with the shared insertion/full-result helper, not a placeholder-only equality. Use requireTestCondition for new semantic transition waits: recheck the same current postcondition after a deadline and retain terminal hierarchy/screenshot on failure, as with control lookups. A timeout assertion containing only debugDescription can omit a failure screenshot. Model flags alone do not prove the native consumer received the same environment: compare List selection state and EditButton appearance with actual binding callbacks; supply one owned edit-mode binding at the consumers rather than ignoring legitimate deselection events.
rules.keyboard_and_scroll: Use shared keyboard and reveal handling; retain explicit postconditions for optional transient UI. Keyboard query count/exists alone is not visibility: the OS can retain a zero-height offscreen node. Use object isHittable (false when missing/offscreen) without a separate exists-to-frame dereference. Do not put hittable in matching predicates. A waiter observation timeout is not a current-state verdict: before failing, recheck the same keyboard-closed or unique-actionable dismissal postcondition; never bypass uniqueness or actual keyboard closure.
rules.environment: Check actual fixtures, services, onboarding and dependencies, including simulator team/App ID/bundle consistency and the remote consumer’s shared-data context, before long UI work. After the final common-helper or case edit, rerun syntax, complete UI case-manifest/selection validation, query lint and workflow dispatch-choice coverage before dispatch. Helpers must not start with the XCTest test prefix; a previous pre-edit check is not evidence for changed source.
rules.first_failure_evidence: Compare hierarchy, recording and coordinates before changing an interaction; capture remote-process logs during the test because runner cleanup can stop its simulator; retain bounded persistent probes and repair missing diagnostics before another attempt. Compare the terminal failure capture as well as the immediate transition capture; a transient spinner does not prove persistent loading. If synthesized pointer coordinates already hit the actual unique control, do not try another tap variant: classify the remaining cause as undetermined and observe binding setters/state/lifecycle and numeric input events before changing behavior.
rules.failure_classification: Separate app defects, harness defects, environment failures and inspection failures; count repeat attempts.
rules.runtime_warnings: A passed assertion does not dispose of application runtime warnings.
rules.device_evidence: Simulator checks do not prove actual audio, notification delivery, re-signing or device permissions.
